<DefineConstants>$(DefineConstants);ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

---

### 4. `LibA.csproj` — Unquoted `Condition` attribute (AP-02)
**File:** `LibA.csproj`, line 13

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
```

The condition value is not quoted. If `$(Configuration)` is ever empty (e.g., during evaluation or restore), this evaluates to ` == Debug`, which MSBuild treats as a syntax error or unexpected match. This is a correctness bug.

**Fix:** Quote both sides:
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
```

---

### 5. `LibA.csproj` — Self-referencing `<MSBuild>` publish target (AP-22 / double build)
**File:** `LibA.csproj`, lines 43–45

```xml
<Target Name="PublishOnBuild" AfterTargets="Build">
  <MSBuild Projects="$(MSBuildProjectFullPath)" Targets="Publish" Properties="_IsPublishing=true" />
</Target>
```

This re-invokes the same project with an extra global property (`_IsPublishing=true`), which forks a **second project instance**. Both instances write to the same `OutputPath`/`IntermediateOutputPath`, creating a race condition (double writes, intermittent failures). It also doubles build time for LibA on every build.

**Fix:** Use `DependsOnTargets` or `AfterTargets` chaining within the same instance rather than a recursive `<MSBuild>` call. If publish-on-build is truly needed:
```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <BuildDependsOn>$(BuildDependsOn);PublishOnBuild</BuildDependsOn>
</PropertyGroup>
<Target Name="PublishOnBuild" DependsOnTargets="Publish"
        Condition="'$(DesignTimeBuild)' != 'true'" />
```

---

### 6. `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj` — Wrong F# compilation order
**File:** `BrokenOrder.fsproj`, lines 7–9

```xml
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />   ← depends on Domain
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />     ← defines types
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

F# compilation order is **defined by the order of `<Compile>` items**. `Services.fs` opens `BrokenOrder.Domain` but is listed *before* `Domain.fs`. This will fail with an unresolved module error. Compare with the correctly ordered `OrderService.fsproj` (Domain → Services → Program).

**Fix:**
```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
  <Compile Include="Services.fs" />
  <Compile Include="Program.fs" />
</ItemGroup>
```

---

## 🟡 Warnings (anti-patterns that should be fixed)

### 7. `Directory.Build.props` — Analyzer package missing `PrivateAssets="all"` (AP-16)
**File:** `Directory.Build.props`, lines 16–18

```xml
<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556" />
```

Analyzer packages should declare `PrivateAssets="all"` to prevent them from leaking transitively to downstream consumers. Without it, any project that consumes LibA or LibB as a NuGet package will also get StyleCop enforced on them — almost certainly unintended.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556">
  <PrivateAssets>all</PrivateAssets>
  <IncludeAssets>runtime; build; native; contentfiles; analyzers</IncludeAssets>
</PackageReference>
```

---

### 8. `LibA.csproj` — Hardcoded absolute Windows `OutputPath` (AP-05)
**File:** `LibA.csproj`, line 8

```xml
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibA</OutputPath>
```

This is a hard-coded Windows path. It will fail or produce unexpected results on Linux/macOS CI agents and for any developer whose machine doesn't have a `C:\builds` directory. Also duplicated pattern in LibB (line 8).

**Fix:** Use relative paths or configurable properties:
```xml
<OutputPath>$(RepoRoot)artifacts\bin\LibA\</OutputPath>
```

---

### 9. `LibB.csproj` — Hardcoded absolute Windows `OutputPath` (AP-05)
**File:** `LibB.csproj`, line 8

Same issue as LibA: `C:\builds\output\LibB`. See fix above.

---

### 10. `LibA.csproj` — Legacy assembly `<Reference>` with `<HintPath>` to a `packages\` folder (AP-09)
**File:** `LibA.csproj`, lines 27–30

```xml
<Reference Include="Newtonsoft.Json">
  <HintPath>..\packages\Newtonsoft.Json.13.0.3\lib\net6.0\Newtonsoft.Json.dll</HintPath>
</Reference>
```

This is a legacy `packages.config`-style reference pointing to a `packages\` folder that almost certainly doesn't exist in this SDK-style project. SDK-style projects use `<PackageReference>`, not assembly `<Reference>`. This will cause a build warning or runtime `FileNotFoundException`.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
```

---

### 11. `LibA.csproj` — Redundant `<Compile Include>` for SDK-globbed file (AP-10)
**File:** `LibA.csproj`, lines 21–24

```xml
<Compile Include="Class1.cs" />
<Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
```

SDK-style projects automatically include all `*.cs` files. The explicit `<Compile Include="Class1.cs" />` creates a **duplicate item** (CS2002 warning). The metadata should be set with `Update` alone in a separate `<ItemGroup>`.

**Fix:** Remove the `Include` line and keep only:
```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
</ItemGroup>
```

---

### 12. `LibA.csproj` — Custom target missing `Inputs`/`Outputs` (incremental build breakage)
**File:** `LibA.csproj`, lines 32–34

```xml
<Target Name="PrintVersion" BeforeTargets="Build">
  <Exec Command="echo Building version 1.0.0" />
</Target>
```

This target has no `Inputs`/`Outputs`, so it runs on every single build — even no-op rebuilds. While it's just an `echo`, this pattern signals a broken incremental build and sets a bad precedent.

**Fix:** Either add `Inputs`/`Outputs` for proper incrementality, or if it's truly diagnostic, gate it behind a condition:
```xml
<Target Name="PrintVersion" BeforeTargets="Build"
        Condition="'$(DesignTimeBuild)' != 'true'">
```

## 🔵 Suggestions (style & maintainability improvements)

### 13. No Central Package Management (CPM)
Package versions are scattered across individual files (`Directory.Build.props` and `LibA.csproj`). For a multi-project solution, centralizing versions in a `Directory.Packages.props` file with `<ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>` prevents version drift.

### 14. F# projects not included in solution file
`StyleIssues.sln` only contains LibA and LibB. The two F# projects under `fsharp/` are not part of the solution, which means `dotnet build StyleIssues.sln` won't build them, and they won't receive solution-level `Configuration`/`Platform` global properties.

### 15. `LibA.csproj` — Hardcoded version string in target
The `echo Building version 1.0.0` in `PrintVersion` is a magic string that will become stale. Consider using `$(Version)` or `$(AssemblyVersion)` instead.
